raw:
I answered from prior knowledge of how NAS-Bench-201 cells behave, not from running anything, so these are rough estimates.

The main reasoning: removing an edge or switching to a weaker operation matters most when that edge is the only strong path or when the parent is redundant. Edits that make the cell disconnected, or that take away a parallel route, tend to interact strongly. Many of these claims have no obvious reason to hold consistently across all three datasets, so most estimates sit low.
